strengths: Does not claim all konbini are 24 hours.
Seven-Eleven 2026 hours change is hedged (“on the order of,” “around 6%,” figures will move).
1974 Seven-Eleven Tokyo opening and later 24-hour competition are consistent with chain history.
FTC point is correctly modal: indicated, could, some conditions—not a fake ban on 24-hour stores.
verified: Japan’s first Seven-Eleven opened in Tokyo in 1974 with hours closer to 7 a.m.–11 p.m.
24-hour operation followed in the mid-1970s and became a competitive urban promise.
2019 franchisee/headquarters conflict over mandatory 24-hour opening was national news.
JFTC later flagged that forcing 24-hour operation could raise Antimonopoly Act concerns in some franchise conditions.
Seven-Eleven Japan’s 2026 public comments described on the order of about 1,400 domestic stores (~6%) with changed hours, including overnight closures—figures move.
questionable: 2024 reporting that stores not operating 24 hours had grown into a “noticeable minority” across major chains (no chain named, no figure; 7-Eleven’s later ~6% is a small share).
Closing windows “often adjustable in the late-night to early-morning range” (true of some tested patterns, not a uniform rule).
unsupported: A konbini after the last train reliably includes a customer bathroom.
Fever medicine / children’s medicine as a standard late-night konbini purchase.
needs_source: Any future exact percentage of non-24h stores for Lawson, FamilyMart, or the sector as a whole.

issues.problem: Bathroom is stated as part of the missed-train kit. That is not generally true.
issues.suggestion: Drop bathroom from the guaranteed list; hedge if mentioned.

issues.problem: Presents OTC pediatric/fever medicine as ordinary konbini inventory. Unsupported as a general fact.
issues.suggestion: Delete or hedge; do not invent drugstore-level stock.

issues.problem: Qualitative industry claim adjacent to a specific 7-Eleven 2026 number can be misread as one statistic.
issues.suggestion: Separate chain-specific 2026 hedge from a non-numeric “more flexible closing since ~2019.”
